description:
**Nine scenarios have a `## Downstream results` section and all nine are empty — while the runs that would fill them have already happened.**

koine's scenarios are pressure tests: each names participants, drives them over real links, and records what broke. The intake row `79` invented exists so a scenario can carry what happened when someone actually ran it downstream. `grep -c '## Downstream results' scenarios/*.md` returns **0 out of 9**.

The runs exist. `agora:75-encode-scenarios-as-kcs` and `agora:76-run-kcs-over-live-links` both merged; `console/evidence/kcs-live-run.json` holds the output, and koine's own ratification gate CITES that file. So koine is already depending on a downstream run whose results it never wrote down.

**This is the cheap half of Phase 2.** Phase 2 — downstream adoption — is marked partial because the implementing surfaces are real but nothing came back. Recording the results is mechanical: read the evidence, write what each scenario's legs did, name what broke. It needs no new thinking and it is what the ratification ladder reads.

**`scenarios/README.md` is wrong in the same direction and should be fixed here.** Its KCS-encoding column reads `⬜ planned` nine times; all nine encodings exist at `agora/console/src/kcs/scenarios/`. `ROADMAP.md` then restates the error — *"today it reads `planned` eight times and `exists` zero"* — so a false column propagated into a second document, which is exactly how the portfolio's roadmaps decayed.
warmup: ls scenarios/*.md | head -12; grep -c '## Downstream results' scenarios/*.md | head -12
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('../agora/console/evidence/kcs-live-run.json'));print(type(d), list(d)[:8] if isinstance(d,dict) else len(d))"

userStories.title: Each scenario records what its downstream run actually did
acceptanceCriteria: Every scenario that has been run downstream gains a populated `## Downstream results` section — which participants ran, over what links, what passed, and what broke.

Content comes from `agora`'s recorded evidence, not from re-reasoning about what should have happened. A scenario that was never run says so plainly rather than being left blank, since blank is indistinguishable from unrun today.
A break found downstream is carried as a FINDING with an id, in the shape the scenarios already use for deltas. A pressure test whose breaks are not written down did not pressure-test anything.
Where the evidence is insufficient to say what a leg did, record that gap rather than inferring. The value here is that the section is trustworthy, not that it is full.
userStories.notes: All 10 scenarios now carry a populated `## Downstream results` section; `grep -c '## Downstream results' scenarios/*.md` went 0/9 -> 10 scenario files + README. Content read off agora/console/evidence/kcs-live-run.json (evidence_id sha256-2d9e6c43..., generated 2026-08-24, kcs_version 0.3.0, 9 scenarios, 19/32 live = 59%, verdict partial-live, transport_failures []) plus the encodings at agora/console/src/kcs/scenarios/. 11 findings recorded as DR-1...DR-11, each defined once in the document it bites and indexed in scenarios/README.md; kft-resume-checkpoint.md states plainly it was never encoded and never run. Gates: node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs green (47 files, 896 relative links, 3 status tables match); node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs --ratchet --base main green (0 dead vs 0 on main).

userStories.title: The KCS-encoding column stops lying, in both files
acceptanceCriteria: `scenarios/README.md`'s KCS-encoding column reflects the nine encodings that exist at `agora/console/src/kcs/scenarios/`. It currently reads `⬜ planned` nine times.
`ROADMAP.md`'s restatement of that column is corrected too. The false value propagated from one document into another, which is the specific decay mode this portfolio has just spent an audit on.
Each entry points at the encoding it refers to, so the claim is checkable rather than asserted.
A note records that these two files must agree, and which is the source. Two registers disagreeing about the same fact is a failure this repo's own preamble says has already cost real decisions.
userStories.notes: scenarios/README.md KCS-encoding column now reads exists 9x + absent 1x (was planned 9x); each cell names its encoding file under agora/console/src/kcs/scenarios/ (worlds-to-fabric.ts, media-transform.ts, kmi-otio-roundtrip.ts, finetune.ts, finetune-multimodal.ts, producer-exhaust-finetune.ts, live-schema-mutation.ts, multi-authority.ts, format-stress.ts) plus its scenario id, run date 2026-08-24, and any DR finding that qualifies it. kft-resume-checkpoint.md is 'absent' (no encoding, no owner, DR-11). ROADMAP.md Phase F4's two table rows + its 'nothing was recorded back' bullet + the Phase 1 'all nine sections are empty' caveat all corrected. New note: scenarios/README.md is the register of record, ROADMAP restates it, and both derive from the downstream artifacts. Gates: node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs green (47 files, 918 relative links, 3 status tables match); node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs --ratchet --base main green (0 dead vs 0 on main). Commit efeebed.

userStories.title: What the results change is followed through
acceptanceCriteria: Any finding recorded in US-1 that bears on a spec's promotability is reflected in that spec's open questions or its named gate — the results are an input to the ratification ladder, not an archive.
Where a downstream run demonstrates a clause works as specified, say so. Ratification needs positive evidence and this is where it comes from.

Coordinate with `83-promote-kgp` rather than duplicating it: that tasklist owns KGP's promotion, this one owns the evidence trail. If the results change KGP's verdict, note it there rather than promoting from here.
userStories.notes: Every DR finding bearing on promotability is now in the spec's gate section or open questions, plus the positive evidence. KINP: kcs:worlds-to-fabric's fully-live 3/3 pass observed firewall_holds + two no_sameas_across_worlds probes + deltas A/C; predates ADR-0012 so MA-1..MA-4 unaffected. KGP: SS3.3 claims_converge and SS7's two egress refusals held, but DR-3 (R3 projection round-trip unencoded) leaves the fixture gate where it was - NOT promoted here, promotion stays with 87-kgp-projection-reader-and-roundtrip (AC-3). KMI: DR-4 - artefact gate met by count not content, M-1 unexercised. KCB: DR-7/DR-8 green-over-blocking-deltas stated as the reading rule; DR-12 - fourth count's scenario unencoded. KFT: five SS4.2 refusals observed; DR-5/DR-6/DR-11. KCS: nine documents parse+replay (deltas M/O/N/P); DR-10 into SS7.1/SS7.2 + pressure test as a qualification on the existing re-validation not a second gate, DR-2 into SS7.3. Six dated Editorial changelog entries, no clause/status/version moved. Registers updated: specs/README.md, docs/reference/promotability.md (6 rows + both cross-cutting facts + ranking), ROADMAP.md, CLAUDE.md. Gates observed GREEN: node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs OK - 48 markdown files, 1010 relative links checked, all 3 status tables match their headers; node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs --ratchet --base main -> 0 dead vs 0 on main; check-schemas OK; check-registry OK; check-tasklist-categories OK (5 tasklists); bash .chief/verify.sh --run over the 10 changed files -> 'all selected gates green - allowing merge'. Base integration done first this iteration: rebased 5 commits onto main @da48d29 (conflicts in .chief/state/* resolved to this run's state, scenarios/README.md table merged keeping main's 11th row + this branch's encoding column), then commit 2257748 gave the 11th scenario (kcb-subscription-firehose.md, landed on main) its own '## Downstream results' section as DR-12 and corrected every ten->eleven count.
